title: System and methods for audio data analysis and tagging
related_application_signals: claims benefit of US provisional application 63/163,321 filed 2021-03-19

source_provenance.note: Ephemeral request-token parameters are intentionally not persisted.

classification_signals: G10L17/14 speaker recognition or speaker-related audio processing
G06F40/279 natural-language entity or semantic processing
G10L21/028 audio or speech signal processing
publicly_described_functional_concepts: cloud or distributed processing of large audio collections
machine-learning transcription and translation within one analytic environment
combining outputs from multiple models using confidence information
suggested tags that require analyst review before becoming accepted links
linking reviewed entities to graph or knowledge-management objects
audio and transcript triage based on relevance, recency, status, or tracked-object hits
user feedback on transcription, translation, acoustic processing, and tagging
interface views combining audio playback, transcript review, model confidence, tags, and graph context
speaker separation or diarization as an audio-organization concept

scope_model.analysis_loop: ingest authorized audio -> generate transcript/translation candidates -> attach confidence -> extract candidate entities -> present suggestions -> require human review -> link approved non-sensitive objects -> collect feedback -> evaluate/update models
building_patterns_relevant_to_independen: use pluggable transcription and translation providers behind model adapters
preserve model-specific confidence and provenance before any fusion step
treat extracted entities as proposals rather than facts
place a human approval boundary before graph/object linking
store accepted tags separately from raw model suggestions
use anonymous speaker labels for diarization by default
maintain reversible links from transcript spans to source timestamps
keep feedback datasets versioned and separate from production model state
expose confidence, model version, and provenance in the analyst interface
apply retention, access-control, and audit policy at ingestion rather than after analysis

independent_claim_themes: audio processing with multiple machine-learning outputs and confidence-aware transcript generation
entity extraction followed by a user interface that presents suggested tags
human selection that links accepted entities with stored audio/transcript records and tracked objects
interface organization combining transcript review, audio playback, suggestions, and confidence information
speaker-related acoustic processing appears in dependent-claim themes and is treated as a privacy-sensitive boundary signal rather than a default implementation pattern
claim_scope_signals.legal_scope_rule: Patent scope depends on the controlling claims, prosecution history, legal status, and jurisdiction. This record is an engineering research abstraction only.

family_signals.territorial_status_rule: Do not infer worldwide rights or freedom to operate from this US publication; recheck the relevant national or regional registers before legal or commercial decisions.

use_for: authorized meeting or media transcription workflows

design_divergence_defaults: use independently selected model orchestration and confidence-fusion logic
use a proposal/review/accept lifecycle rather than automatically converting extracted entities into authoritative objects
default speaker handling to anonymous diarization rather than biometric identification
separate source media storage from derived transcript, translation, graph, and feedback stores
make provenance, model versions, and confidence visible and auditable
enforce least-privilege access and explicit retention policies for audio and derived data
require legal/privacy review before deploying person-linked audio analytics

mandatory_safety_boundaries: no biometric voiceprint identification by default
no person tracking across unrelated datasets
privacy and legal review for person-linked deployments
